setup.title: Input
setup.help: Which mic is plugged in, and how the pedal treats the voice before any effects.

fields.label: Input
fields.help: Which input the pedal listens to. Match it to the microphone you plug in, so the pedal can tune its preamp for that type. USB Left/Right takes sound from a computer instead.

fields.label: RoomSense
fields.help: The two small microphones built into the pedal. Ambient picks up the room for your headphone mix. Ambient/Auto also listens to the music to work out its key, so harmonies can follow the band. Voice uses them instead of a microphone, and is heard in headphones only.

fields.label: Aux In Type
fields.help: What is plugged into the Aux socket. Live suits a band or instrument feed, Tracks suits pre-recorded music you sing along to, and Monitor lets you hear it without using it to work out the key.

fields.label: Tone Style
fields.help: Automatic EQ, compression and gating on the lead voice. Normal suits most singers. The NG versions leave the gate off, so a very quiet voice is never cut off.

fields.label: Pitch Correction
fields.help: Gentle automatic tuning applied to everything you sing. Off leaves the voice untouched; higher amounts pull harder towards the nearest note, up to a hard Auto-Tune effect.
fields.note: Global: runs on every preset, even with every effect switched off. The Editor shows it under HardTune.

setup.title: Output
setup.help: How sound leaves the pedal: to the PA, headphones and USB.

fields.label: Output
fields.help: How the two XLR outputs are used. Stereo sends the whole sound to both. Mono sends your dry voice out Left and all effects out Right, for a sound engineer who wants them separate. Dual Mono sends voice and effects out Left, and anything from Aux out Right. With only one cable in Left, Mono means no effects are heard.

fields.label: USB Out
fields.help: Level of the sound the pedal sends to a computer over USB.

fields.label: Vocal Cancel
fields.help: Tries to remove the lead vocal from music coming in on Aux, so you can sing along karaoke style. How well it works varies from song to song.

fields.label: Headphone Limit
fields.help: Where the headphone limiter starts holding the volume back, to protect your ears.

fields.label: Lead Mute
fields.help: Removes your own voice from the output, leaving only the processed sounds such as harmonies.

fields.label: Aux to Main Out
fields.help: Whether music coming in on Aux is also sent to the PA, or stays in your headphones only.

setup.title: Global
setup.help: Settings that stay put when you change presets.

fields.label: Global Key
fields.help: Keeps the key you set for harmonies when you change presets, instead of each preset bringing its own.

fields.label: Global Tempo
fields.help: Keeps the tempo you tapped when you change presets, so delays stay in time from song to song.

fields.label: Mic Boost
fields.help: Extra gain for quiet sources. Off suits a line-level source such as a wireless receiver; Low or High suit a microphone plugged straight in. Watch the pedal's input light while singing loudly: it should never sit red.

fields.label: Loop Input
fields.help: What the looper records: your voice with its effects, the Aux input, or both together.

fields.label: Undo
fields.help: Keeps the last loop layer undoable. On gives 15 seconds of loop time; Off doubles it to 30 seconds.

fields.label: Loop Feedback
fields.help: How loud the existing layers stay when you record another one. Around 90% stops a loop getting louder with every pass.

setup.title: System
setup.help: The screen, tuning and how the pedal itself behaves.

fields.label: LCD Contrast
fields.help: How dark the pedal's own screen looks. Adjust it for the light you play in.

fields.label: Tune Reference
fields.help: The tuning everything is measured against. 440.0 Hz is standard; change it to match instruments tuned elsewhere.

fields.label: Up/Dn Function
fields.help: What pressing both footswitches together does: start looping, or set the key for harmonies.

fields.label: Pitch Pipe Level
fields.help: Volume of the reference note in the pedal's Practice screen.

fields.label: Lead Delay
fields.help: Delays your dry voice very slightly so harmonies line up exactly with it. None is the most immediate. Voice Sync always aligns by the same amount. Auto aligns by how many effects are running.

fields.label: RoomSense Low Cut
fields.help: Cuts low rumble picked up by the pedal's built-in room microphones, such as stage noise or air conditioning.

setup.title: Switch-3
setup.help: What the optional three-button footswitch does. Switches 1-3 apply when Control is Custom.

fields.label: Control
fields.help: Whether an optional three-button footswitch runs the looper with fixed functions, or the three assignments you choose below.

fields.label: Harm Moment
fields.help: Harmony sounds only while a footswitch is held down, instead of switching on and off with each press.

fields.label: Delay Moment
fields.help: Delay sounds only while a footswitch is held down.

fields.label: Switch 1
fields.help: What the first button on an optional three-button footswitch does. It applies when Control is set to Custom.

fields.label: Switch 2
fields.help: What the second button on an optional three-button footswitch does. It applies when Control is set to Custom.

fields.label: Switch 3
fields.help: What the third button on an optional three-button footswitch does. It applies when Control is set to Custom.

setup.title: Mic Control
setup.help: What the buttons on a TC-Helicon MP-75 or MP-76 mic do. The four MP-76 buttons apply when MP-76 Control is Custom.

fields.label: MP-75 Control
fields.help: What the button on a TC-Helicon MP-75 microphone does.

fields.label: MP-76 Control
fields.help: Whether a TC-Helicon MP-76 microphone uses its standard button layout, or the four assignments you choose below.

fields.label: MP-76 Top
fields.help: What the top button on an MP-76 microphone does. It applies when MP-76 Control is set to Custom.

fields.label: MP-76 Bottom
fields.help: What the bottom button on an MP-76 microphone does. It applies when MP-76 Control is set to Custom.

fields.label: MP-76 Left
fields.help: What the left button on an MP-76 microphone does. It applies when MP-76 Control is set to Custom.

fields.label: MP-76 Right
fields.help: What the right button on an MP-76 microphone does. It applies when MP-76 Control is set to Custom.

blocks.title: Harmony
blocks.help: Adds sung harmony lines above or below the lead.

blocks.title: Doubling
blocks.help: Stacks copies of the voice for a thicker, produced sound.

blocks.title: Reverb
blocks.help: Sense of room, from a small studio to an arena.

blocks.title: Delay
blocks.help: Repeats, or echoes, of the voice.

blocks.title: Voice Modulation
blocks.help: Chorus, flange and stranger movement effects.

blocks.title: HardTune
blocks.help: Pitch correction, from gentle to the hard Auto-Tune sound.

blocks.title: Megaphone & Distortion
blocks.help: Megaphone, radio, phone and amp-style distortion. Called Transducer on the pedal.

params.label: Voicing
params.help: Which harmony lines the pedal sings with you: above, below, or both, and how many voices.

params.label: Key
params.help: The song's key, so the harmonies stay in tune. Auto follows what the pedal hears you sing.

params.label: Scale
params.help: Which scale the harmony notes are picked from inside the key. The variations shift a few notes each, so try them if a harmony sounds sour.

params.label: Level
params.help: How loud the harmony voices are against your own.

params.label: Style
params.help: How many copies of your voice are added and how closely they follow it. Wider styles spread them left and right.

params.label: Level
params.help: How loud the copies are against your own voice.

params.label: Style
params.help: The kind of space: plates and rooms are tight, halls and arenas are big.

params.label: Decay
params.help: How long the reverb tail lasts after you stop singing.

params.label: Level
params.help: How loud the reverb is against your voice.

params.label: Style
params.help: The echo pattern: single repeats, rhythmic ones that follow the tempo, or ping-pong between left and right.

params.label: Time L (ms)
params.help: How long before the echo repeats on the left, in milliseconds. Only styles that don't follow the tempo use it.

params.label: Time R (ms)
params.help: How long before the echo repeats on the right, in milliseconds. Only styles that don't follow the tempo use it.

params.label: Feedback
params.help: How many times each echo repeats before fading away.

params.label: Filter
params.help: The tone of the repeats. Tape and analog styles get duller with each one, like older echo machines.

params.label: Level
params.help: How loud the echoes are against your voice.

params.label: Style
params.help: The kind of movement added: chorus, flanging, rotating speaker and stranger effects.

params.label: Level
params.help: How loud the modulation effect is against your voice.

params.label: Style
params.help: How hard your pitch is pushed to the nearest note, from gentle correction to the hard Auto-Tune sound.

params.label: Shift (semitones)
params.help: Moves your voice up or down in semitones.

params.label: Gender
params.help: Changes the character of the voice: lower sounds bigger and deeper, higher sounds thinner and brighter.

params.label: Style
params.help: The voice it imitates: megaphone, radio, telephone or a guitar amp.

params.label: Drive
params.help: How hard the sound is pushed, from slight grit to full distortion.

params.label: Filter
params.help: The tone of the distortion, from thin and boxy to full and open.

params.label: Tempo (BPM)
params.help: The song's tempo. Delay styles that follow the beat use it, so their echoes stay in time.
